narrative.overview:
Golden Spades reads as a card table dressed for an upscale night: cream card-stock paper, deep emerald felt, and warm gold foil, with a serif marquee typeface standing in for the pit boss's signage and a clean grotesque carrying everything you actually have to read. The system is deliberately warm and daytime-legible rather than nocturnal-neon-casino -- it is a real neighborhood barbershop borrowing the iconography of cards and chips (suit pips, 'Ace Experience,' 'Royal Flush' package names), not a Vegas pastiche. It is the confirmed opposite number to the client's other shop, Scissorhands Barbershop, whose system is dark red/black grunge with a spinning barber-pole motif and a bold condensed display face -- nothing in that system may bleed into this one.

Flat by construction: no drop shadows anywhere. Depth comes from a thin gold-foil frame around every panel and from a small suit-pip mark tucked in a card-frame's corner, echoing the index pip on a real playing card. Selection and emphasis are never conveyed by a border alone -- a defect the client explicitly reported and that this system now treats as an invariant: a selected state gets a visibly thicker gold border, a solid gold-tinted fill, and a small gold checkmark badge.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, deepened cream/tan base with deep emerald felt bands for header/footer/hero contrast
Serif-italic display type (Playfair Display) for headings and CTA labels, clean sans (Jost) for body text
Rounded playing-card panels (1.25rem corners) with a slim translucent gold frame, never a drop shadow
Small suit-pip glyphs as the system's one recurring decorative signature
Pill-shaped buttons; gold fill for the primary action, felt-green fill for the secondary action
Selection state always shows all three signals together: border, fill, and badge

rules.name: The Single Loud Color Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only saturated color in the system; every other hue stays muted, which is what makes gold register as premium instead of noisy.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: This system never uses box-shadow for elevation. A card reads as raised because Ivory is lighter than the Cream/Cream-Dim it sits on and is framed by a gold border. The one exception is the selection glow ring, which is a state signal, not ambient elevation.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: A selected interactive card must show all three of border-weight, fill, and badge together, never border alone. This was a confirmed defect (users could not tell what they had selected) and regressing to border-only is a functional bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Italic-for-Voice Rule
rules.body: Italic Playfair Display marks a line as the brand speaking (eyebrow taglines, button labels, footer headings) rather than describing content. Section titles and card titles stay upright.

dos: Do keep gold as the only saturated color in the system; every other hue stays muted.
Do signal a selected/active interactive state with border-weight, fill, and badge together.
Do use Playfair Display italic for brand-voice moments and upright Playfair Display for section/card titles.
Do keep every card-style panel flat with a gold-tinted border instead of a shadow.
donts: Don't introduce drop shadows for elevation anywhere in this system.
Don't borrow Scissorhands' visual vocabulary: no dark red/black grunge palette, no Anton display face, no spinning barber-pole stripe, no diagonal-cut sharp corners, no grain texture.
Don't rely on a border-color change alone to indicate selection.
Don't add a second saturated accent color; reach for a neutral or a Gold variant first.
